sender.en: Someone you met on social media or a marriage site who builds a close relationship

name.en: Love or marriage scam: “I'm in financial trouble, help me and we'll marry”

how.en: Someone you meet online builds trust over weeks or months, talks about marriage or a future together, and then has money problems or a business that needs funding. They ask you to transfer money, sometimes to take loans in your name, promising to pay it back. In 2026 an Abu Dhabi court ordered a man to repay Dh194,000 to a woman he deceived through a social media relationship, and a Dubai woman won a case after losing nearly Dh1 million to a man who promised marriage and was already married.

text.en: A new online contact becomes close and talks about marriage.
They have money trouble or a project that needs funding.
They promise to repay you, and the requests keep coming.

Habibti, I'm so embarrassed to ask but the bank froze my account and I have to pay the contractor this week or I lose the whole project. Can you transfer AED 25,000? When it's done I will return everything and we can finally tell our families.

en: met him on social media and he asked for money
he promised to marry me and i transferred money
took a loan for my online partner
he said he was in financial difficulty and needed help
found out he was already married after i sent the money
Someone you have never met in person asking for money.
Talk of marriage early, followed by money problems.
Requests to take loans or transfer to other people's accounts.
Never send money to someone you only know online.
Talk to family or friends before any transfer.
If you have paid, keep the messages and bank records and report it to the police and your bank.

sources.title: UAE Court Orders Dh194,000 Repayment in Social Media Romance Scam Case
Nearly Dh1 million lost in marriage scam: UAE woman wins case with WhatsApp messages

story.en: A man formed an emotional relationship with a woman through social media and told her he was in serious financial difficulty. She transferred money to him and later realised she had been scammed. He was convicted of fraud, and an Abu Dhabi court ordered him to pay her Dh194,000.
